items.title: Multi-Model Machine & Deep Learning Framework for Landslide Susceptibility Mapping
items.description: A comprehensive multi-model comparative study evaluating 10 statistical, machine learning, deep learning, and ensemble models for landslide susceptibility mapping in Nepal's fragile eastern Chure region.
responsibilities: Mapped and verified a field-validated inventory of 176 landslide locations across five watersheds using satellite imagery and GIS.
Built, optimized, and compared 10 distinct predictive algorithms across Statistical (FR), Machine Learning (RF, XGBoost, LightGBM, SVM, LR), and Deep Learning (ANN, DNN, CNN, LSTM) frameworks.
Authored and published the peer-reviewed research paper independently in Discover Hazards (Springer).
items.body:
### Project Overview
Landslides pose severe threats to infrastructure and ecosystems in the active Sub-Himalayan (Chure) zone of Nepal[cite: 2, 4]. This independent research project was designed to rigorously evaluate whether complex Deep Learning (DL) architectures provide predictive advantages over classical tree-based Machine Learning (ML) ensemble models when applied to data-limited, tabular geomorphic conditioning factors in steep mountain environments[cite: 2, 4].

The study covered five hydrologically connected watersheds spanning **305.14 km²** across Morang, Ilam, and Dhankuta districts in Koshi Province[cite: 5].

---

### Key Methodology & Workflow
* **Inventory & Factors:** A field-verified inventory of 176 landslide events[cite: 6, 8] evaluated against 12 spatial conditioning factors (slope, aspect, elevation, curvatures, TWI, SPI, soil, lithology, land use, and distances to roads/rivers)[cite: 7, 8].
* **Model Implementation:** Implemented 10 models—Frequency Ratio (FR)[cite: 2, 8], Random Forest (RF), XGBoost, LightGBM, SVM, Logistic Regression[cite: 2, 9], Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Deep Neural Network (DNN), 1D-CNN, and LSTM[cite: 2, 9, 10].
* **Ensemble Fusion:** Developed a **Top-3 ML Ensemble** combining RF, XGBoost, and LightGBM to produce spatially coherent, low-error susceptibility maps[cite: 2, 10, 15].

---

### Major Findings
1. **Tree-Based Superiority:** Tree-based ensemble models achieved the best performance, with **Random Forest leading at Test AUC = 0.928**, followed by XGBoost (0.881) and LightGBM (0.844)[cite: 2, 12].
2. **Deep Learning Constraints:** Deep learning architectures (ANN: 0.773, CNN: 0.766, DNN: 0.765, LSTM: 0.622) underperformed relative to ML ensembles due to the constraints of limited sample size on tabular data[cite: 2, 12, 13, 19].
3. **Lowest Prediction Error:** The Top-3 Ensemble achieved the lowest Mean Absolute Error (**MAE = 0.238**) and produced the most geomorphically consistent hazard zoning[cite: 2, 15, 19].
4. **Hazard Exposure:** **22.7% of the total watershed area** was classified under High to Very High landslide susceptibility zones, driven heavily by topographic wetness index (TWI), slope, and weak Siwalik lithology[cite: 2, 15, 18].

---

### Publication & Citation

* **DOI:** [10.1007/s44475-026-00029-0](https://doi.org/10.1007/s44475-026-00029-0)[cite: 2]
